comparison: Perfect agreement on conditional genetic tools (C3-C5, C30-C38). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED and acknowledge high efficiency with appropriate recognition of limitations (leaky expression, incomplete temporal control). OpenEval provides more granular analysis of specific limitations while peer reviewers emphasize 'transparent assessment of variability.'

Strong agreement on CRISPR/Cas9 approach (C39-C46). Both rate as SUPPORTED and acknowledge variable efficiency across genes. OpenEval emphasizes the failure to reproduce some sleep phenotypes and incomplete effectiveness, while peer reviewers note 'concerns about variability' but accept the transparent reporting of limitations.

Complete agreement on improved Cas9 variants (C47-C57). Both rate as SUPPORTED with no significant concerns. OpenEval notes discrepancy between sequencing and imaging-based efficiency estimates, while peer reviewers highlight this as a 'significant technical advance' without questioning the data quality.

Perfect concordance on UNCERTAIN rating for expression profiling (C58-C67). Both identify concerns about accuracy and discrepancies with prior literature. OpenEval explicitly notes speculative explanations and uncertain accuracy, while peer reviewers question 'accuracy of the gene expression approach' and note it is 'complementary' rather than definitive.

Agreement on pilot screen and CNMa identification (C68-C73). Both rate as SUPPORTED despite the Cas9.M9 leaky expression issue. OpenEval emphasizes this limitation undermines confidence in negative results, while peer reviewers accept it as part of 'transparent assessment' and focus on the positive CNMa discovery.

Partial overlap on CNMa findings (C73-C76). OpenEval R5 covers initial CNMa discovery from screen, while peer R6 focuses on the detailed anatomical and functional characterization. Both support the CNMa findings but address different aspects of the same biological discovery.

Strong agreement on CNMa anatomical and functional characterization (C77-C86). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate caution about type I neurons being 'main functional subset,' while peer reviewers fully accept the CNMa function in DN1ps without raising concerns about the anatomical claims.

Significant disagreement on PDF-CNMa relationship (C87-C91). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about speculation, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'the issue regarding opposing effects of PDF signaling and CNMa...still stands.' Peer reviewers question the mechanistic interpretation more strongly than OpenEval.

Agreement on CNMaR findings (C92-C97). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval raises question about which CNMaR-expressing neurons are functionally relevant given broad expression, while peer reviewers accept the data without specific concerns, viewing it as supporting the overall CNMa/CNMaR story.

Disagreement on antagonistic relationship claim (C7-C11). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveats about unclear mechanistic basis, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning the 'opposing effects' interpretation. Both accept the phenotypic data but differ on confidence in the antagonistic relationship conclusion.

OpenEval evaluated background claims about prior CRISPR work and limitations (C1-C2, C12-C14) as SUPPORTED contextual framing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are literature-based contextual claims rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval evaluated background literature claims about neuropeptide research and gaps (C15-C21) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are appropriately cited background claims that frame the study's novelty rather than testable findings.

OpenEval evaluated background claims about Drosophila circadian biology (C22-C29) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are well-established literature-based contextual claims that provide biological background rather than novel experimental findings.
